Evaluate personal and group performance of repertory.

rows.title: Advanced Beginning Ballet
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify advanced beginning ballet vocabulary.
Apply the principles of ballet technique to the execution of advanced beginning ballet barre exercises and center practice.
Perform advanced beginning ballet barre and center exercises with agility.
Perform advanced beginning ballet center combinations integrating connecting and traveling steps.
Apply musicality appropriate to advanced beginning barre exercises, center exercises, and combinations.

rows.title: Beginning Pointe Technique
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify parts of a pointe shoe
Select and fit a pointe shoe according to one's foot structure and technical skill
Identify and perform pre-pointe exercises to develop muscular strength of the feet, ankles and lower legs
Identify and perform elementary pointe vocabulary with correct body alignment, hip to toe placement, and correct balance points
Discuss a brief history of pointe.

rows.title: Advanced Beginning Modern Dance
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and perform advanced beginning modern dance technique, vocabulary, and combinations.
Explain and demonstrate correct body alignment both static and dynamic as it applies to advanced beginning modern dance sequences across the floor.
Identify and perform the elements of an advanced beginning modern dance class to build strength, flexibility, endurance, coordination, and agility.
Perform advanced beginning modern dance technique emphasizing levels and spatial patterns, qualities of movement, use of weight, and musicality.
Identify and discuss important aspects of modern dance history.

rows.title: Dance Improvisation: Group
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the history and development of improvisational movement from the 1950s-1970s.
Integrate improvisational movement techniques with movement compositions.
Perform group improvisations.

rows.title: Intermediate Jazz Dance
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and perform intermediate jazz dance vocabulary, combinations, and technique.
Demonstrate correct body alignment in static and moving positions as it applies to performing intermediate jazz dance combinations.
Differentiate verbally and physically the unique use of space, weight, time, and direction of movement characteristic to intermediate jazz dance.
Perform intermediate jazz movement patterns to introduce rhythmic structure with arms and legs.
Examine the historical evolution of jazz dance styles and innovators.

rows.title: Advanced Beginning African Haitian
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Execute advanced beginning level movement vocabulary utilizing various African Haitian techniques styles.
Identify and perform advanced beginning African Haitian step progressions and choreographies with correct alignment and technique.
Evaluate and perform advanced beginning dance patterns with the appropriate musicality.
Compare dance pioneers and their contributions to African Haitian dance.

rows.title: Advanced Beginning Tap Dance
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Integrate tap movement principles with advanced beginning tap technique.
Describe and demonstrate advanced beginning tap vocabulary.
Relate rhythmic and compositional structure to tap phrases in performance of an advanced beginning tap dance.
Identify early tap dance masters that relate to advanced beginning tap vocabulary.

rows.title: Advanced Beginning Hip Hop Dance
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify advanced beginning-level Hip Hop technique, vocabulary, and combinations.
Demonstrate strength, flexibility, endurance, coordination and agility to perform advanced beginning technique and combinations.
Demonstrate correct body alignment with advanced beginning isolations and shifting of weight.
Perform beginning-level Hip Hop movements in conjunction with the musicality of Hip Hop music and the vocal rhythms.
Identify and discuss important aspects of Hip Hop history from 1990 to the present.

rows.title: Intermediate Ballroom Dance
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Perform the intermediate step variations for various ballroom dances.
Analyze intermediate-level posture fundamentals to leading and following, emphasizing correct connection, frame, and momentum.
Identify musical structure and rhythms for intermediate-level ballroom dance forms.
Discuss the historical development of each dance.

rows.title: Intermediate Salsa and Other Latin Dances
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Perform intermediate steps, step variations, and movement sequences of salsa and selected Latin American social dances.
Analyze and demonstrate intermediate level leading and following techniques including frame, connection, balance and momentum.
Perform intermediate Salsa dance steps that align with rhythm, syncopation and phrasing of the music.

rows.title: Advanced Argentine Tango
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and use advanced Argentine Tango movement vocabulary.
Explain advanced-level frame and connection.
Describe people and places in the world of Argentine Tango today.

rows.title: Yoga Movement
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Perform basic yoga techniques and principles.
Apply musicality to yoga movement sequences.
Integrate yoga combinations with dance elements.

rows.title: Feldenkrais for Dance and Performing Arts
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate a performer's quality of movement as it relates to somatic experience and the expressiveness of their performance.
Summarize benefits of the Feldenkrais Method for performers and relate those benefits to lifelong wellness.
Apply the learning strategies of differentiation and reversibility in relationship to performance, and to adaptation for individual structural differences or injury.
Recognize and evaluate the impact of the performer's relationship to the environment of the play (who is doing what, to whom, to what end).
Command stage as a soloist through spatial orientation and ground forces.

rows.title: Introduction to Chairside Assisting
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Assemble trays of instruments and materials for restorative, fixed prosthodontic and endodontic procedures, and identify their proper sequence of use.
Perform chairside dental assistant procedures and techniques, adhering to state and federal requirements for the management of patient care.
Apply the Centers for Disease Control (CDC) Standard Precautions, utilizing personal protective equipment in every dental situation.

rows.title: Dental Office Management
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Use positive patient rapport for effective patient management during business transactions.
Discuss treatment plan options and informed consent for optimum patient care.
Conduct dental practice business functions, observing state and federal regulations for the provision of dental care.

rows.title: Clinical Dental Assisting Internship
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Perform all registered dental assistant duties outlined by the California Dental Practice Act.
Comply with internship facilities’ infection control and safety guidelines.

rows.title: Radiologic Physics and Equipment
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Select appropriate parameters of radiographic equipment operation to create a diagnostic image.
Apply digital methods of image processing.
Analyze the role of the various circuit components that contribute to x-ray and image production for radiographic/fluoroscopic modalities.

rows.title: Vascular and Interventional Procedures
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe common procedures performed in the angiographic and interventional radiology suites.
Model sterile techniques as applied to angiography and interventional radiography
Consider appropriate uses of equipment and devices used in the interventional radiology suite.
Examine aspects of patient care and safety considerations during interventional radiologic procedures

rows.title: Intermediate Diagnostic Procedures
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate the proper utilization of mobile radiography and C-arm fluoroscopy equipment when conducting extra-departmental radiographic procedures
Demonstrate the steps involved in performing venipuncture in a simulated clinical environment.
Describe the steps involved in performing intermediate radiographic imaging procedures.
Devise techniques for appropriate care and imaging of different patient populations.
Evaluate ethical dilemmas and legal issues that may impact patient care and management

rows.title: Clinical Education in DMI IV
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Appraise communication models for effectiveness in relating to patients and clinical personnel
Relate theoretical principles of Diagnostic Medical Imaging to advanced-level clinical performance and practice.
Model optimal professionalism and ethical behavior as it relates to the clinical environment.
Perform clinical procedures according to established competencies of the Diagnostic Medical Imaging program.
Model optimal radiation safety during procedures in a clinical setting.
Model optimal patient care and safety during procedures in a clinical setting.
Solve problems related to radiologic procedures performed and situations encountered in the clinical setting.

rows.title: ECG Technician I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the anatomy and physiology of the cardiovascular system and the cardiac conduction system.
Analyze electrocardiography waveforms related to the cardiac cycle.
Calculate heart rate and measurements of all waveforms and intervals on the normal and abnormal electrocardiographic readings.
Describe the characteristics of a normal 12-Lead ECG and the characteristics of sinus, atrial, junctional and ventricular dysrhythmias.
Apply the appropriate techniques for the placement of ECG electrodes on a patient to acquire a 12-lead ECG tracing.

rows.title: Echocardiography
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply the knowledge of cardiac anatomy to a beginning cardiac sonographer level identification and assessment of two-dimensional (2D) images in the parasternal long axis, apical views, and subcostal view.
Examine the pulse wave, continuous wave, and color flow patterns associated with normal, stenotic, and regurgitant cardiac findings.
Use formulas and parameters to determine cardiac performance: cardiac output, stroke volume, ejection fraction, cardiac index, valve area, and chamber pressures.

Perform the standard measurements and state the normative values of cardiac chambers, walls, and vessels in the standardized imaging views within the standards of the American Society of Echocardiography.
Integrate knowledge of the pathophysiology of the cardiovascular system to skills performed by the entry-level cardiac sonographer.

rows.title: Political Economy
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the basic principles of economics and political science and integrate them into the analysis of questions about public policy and societal institutions.
Assess the intersection between international politics and economics and understand the effects of politics on economic policy at the state, national, and international levels.
Identify and contrast the structure, strengths and weaknesses of various economic and governmental systems.
Apply modern political economic theory to current socieconomic issues.

rows.title: Economics of the African American Community
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe and analyze the features of classical European and U.S. slavery and its long-term impact on African underdevelopment and on the current economic status of people of African descent living in the African diaspora.
Explain the process by which Black sharecroppers were transformed into a class of "free" Black wage laborers.
Interpret and critically analyze several alternative theories of racial economic inequality.
Assess and critique the market for Black consumer goods and the strengths and weaknesses of Black capitalism.
Analyze housing markets and their imperfections, especially the practice and impact of housing discrimination and residential segregation.

rows.title: Principles of Macroeconomics
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Interpret and analyze domestic and international macroeconomic data.
Apply macroeconomic models to explain economic issues and outcomes.
Analyze the effects of macroeconomic policies.
Describe the institutional structure of a modern capitalist economy, including the public and private sectors

rows.title: Electronics III: Analog Circuits and Practical Applications
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Construct, analyze, and test different configurations of bipolar junction transistors (BJTs), field effect transistors (JFETs), and operational amplifiers.
Formulate test procedures to analyze simple electronic projects and verify how they work.
Integrate the multi-meter, oscilloscope, LCR (inductance L, capacitance C, and resistance R) meter, sweep generator and other instruments into the construction and analysis of electronic circuits.
Trace the signal path for an existing circuit board to create a schematic and bill of materials.

rows.title: Emergency Medical Technician
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply team-based resuscitation and basic life support interventions consistent with evidence-based practice and national EMS guidelines.
Integrate knowledge of human body systems from birth to death into patient assessment within the scope of practice of an emergency medical technician (EMT).
Apply an EMT level assessment to the appropriate management of patients of all age groups with a variety of emergency medical and traumatic conditions.
Analyze the roles and responsibilities of the EMT in routine and specialized EMS incidents.
Emulate a culture of safety, cultural humility, and patient advocacy as a prehospital emergency medical professional.

rows.title: Introduction to EMS
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Examine the major events and issues that have influenced the development and future direction of modern EMS systems in the United States.
Apply medical legal principles to a variety of challenging prehospital situations while guided by national standards and ethical principles of prehospital patient care.
Analyze the key elements of EMS research and its benefits to prehospital emergency care.
Apply principles of prehospital patient assessment, communications, and documentation to current standards in prehospital patient care.
Perform basic and advanced airway techniques within the paramedic scope of practice.

rows.title: Cardiorespiratory Emergencies
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Interpret electrocardiograms of patients presenting with a variety of medical and traumatic emergency conditions.
Correlate patient assessment findings to the differential diagnosis of cardiovascular and respiratory emergencies.
Apply current standards of prehospital care and emergency pharmacology to treat pulmonary and cardiovascular emergencies within the national scope of practice of a paramedic.
Communicate effectively according to standards of the emergency medical services (EMS) profession.

rows.title: Special Populations, EMS Ops
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Integrate assessment findings with principles of epidemiology and pathophysiology to formulate a field impression and implement a treatment plan for an acutely ill or injured patient.
Perform a systematic patient assessment used for patients with special challenges including geriatrics, chronically ill, technology-dependent, abused/neglected, and dying patients.
Analyze the differences in pharmacokinetics, physiology, and psychosocial environment between adult and geriatric patients.
Determine the preferred method of treatment for geriatric patients with common and acute medical and trauma emergencies.

Examine and emulate safe scene practices considering crime scene awareness, transport alternatives, and the need for additional expert resources on routine EMS incidents and multiple casualty incidents.

rows.title: American Literature, Beginnings to Civil War
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify the major genres, themes, and textual concerns of the early American literary period.
Analyze individual texts in relation to the significant historical, cultural, and/or social issues of the early American era.
Analyze the content and formal structures of an early American text.
Integrate textual evidence and literary criticism when writing essays on key works of the early American era.

rows.title: Introduction to Writing Poetry
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compose poems containing basic elements of craft.
Identify basic poetic craft elements in published work.
Analyze how poetic form, content, and style function together.
Appraise works-in-progress, sharing basic-level critiques with peers in constructive ways.

rows.title: Introduction to Literary Magazine
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze and critically discuss pieces submitted for publication in terms of literary merit, at an introductory level.
Analyze and evaluate literary magazines for editorial practices and aesthetic criteria.
Apply junior-level editing and proofreading skills to selected submissions for accuracy.
Employ editorial skills to create a professional quality literary magazine.

rows.title: Survey of World Literature, Part II: Early Modern to the Present
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the major genres, themes, and textual concerns of literature from 1650 to the present.
Analyze individual texts in relation to the significant historical, cultural, and/or social issues from 1650 to the present.
Analyze the content and formal structures of world literature written from 1650 to the present.
Integrate textual evidence and literary criticism when writing essays on key works from 1650 to the present.

rows.title: Science Fiction and Fantasy
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the major themes, scenarios, and textual concerns of science fiction and fantasy.
Analyze individual texts in relation to the significant historical, cultural, and social contexts.
Analyze the content and formal structures of specific science fiction and fantasy works.
Integrate textual evidence and literary criticism when writing essays on key works of science fiction and fantasy.

rows.title: Children's and Young Adult Literature
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Distinguish conventions of children's and young adult literature from those of other literary genres.
Interpret children’s and young adult literature, using tools of literary analysis.
Analyze the historical and social contexts that shape children's and young adult literature.
Integrate textual evidence and literary criticism when writing essays on children's and young adult literature.

rows.title: Video Games and Literature
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe shared themes, narrative structures, and textual concerns in literature and video games.
Analyze literary and gaming methods of storytelling by applying narrative theories.
Evaluate the ways elements of literature and elements of video games engage the same themes.
Integrate textual evidence and literary criticism when writing about key video games and works of literature.

rows.title: Critical Thinking and Writing through Literature
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Critically read, analyze, compare, and evaluate diverse complex literary texts.
Reflect critically on one’s own thought processes to identify and avoid cognitive biases and common fallacies of language and thought.

Compose thesis-driven arguments to suit a variety of rhetorical situations, including interpretation, evaluation, and literary analysis, supporting them with a variety of appropriate textual evidence and examples.
Identify a text's premise(s) and/or assumptions in various social, historical, cultural, psychological, or aesthetic contexts.

Analyze and employ logical and structural methods such as inductive and deductive reasoning, causation, and supporting claims with reasons, evidence, and responding to diverse perspectives and values.
Find, analyze, interpret, and evaluate primary and secondary sources, incorporating them into written work using appropriate documentation format without plagiarism.

Draft and revise writing for style, diction, and tone showing awareness of audience and social context, and the purpose of the specific writing task; engage in a revision process so that language use does not impede clarity or disrupt meaning.
Identify key elements of major genres (including poetry, drama, fiction) in order to analyze and interpret texts.
Define common literary terms and apply these to analysis of specific texts.

rows.title: Introduction to Circuit Analysis Laboratory
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Operate lab equipment for circuit analyses in a safe and proper manner.
Build complex circuits from schematic diagrams.
Experimentally verify Ohm's Law, Kirchoff's Laws, and transient RL/RC/RLC circuits via measurement, hand calculations, and electronic circuit analysis programs.

rows.title: Introduction to Clean and Renewable Energy Laboratory
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze physical phenomena and basic scientific concepts of renewable energy sources and systems.
Calculate basic energy and physics related computations.
Measure and collect data utilizing laboratory equipment.
Set up and perform laboratory experiments analyzing the scientific principles behind utilizing energy sources.
Prepare written laboratory reports focused on empirically verifying theoretical scientific principles and technical aspects of energy systems.
Assess and evaluate critical factors affecting real world applications in clean and renewable energy.

rows.title: Introduction to Environmental Science
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify core scientific principles that relate to human interactions with the environment.
Interpret the scientific evidence underlying the causes and consequences of human impacts on the environment and their implications for societal welfare.
Apply scientific, economic and sociopolitical concepts and models to interpret and analyze environmental issues from various sources.
Integrate principles and methods from the natural sciences, social sciences, and engineering to evaluate and propose sustainable solutions to environmental degradation and resource depletion.
Critique quantitative and qualitative assessments of human environmental impacts and relate them to sustainable lifestyle choices.

rows.title: ESL Introduction to College Reading and Writing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze and interpret a range of authentic expository and narrative low-advanced-level English texts, using a variety of low-advanced reading skills and strategies.
Compose organized and well-supported essays using a low-advanced level of English.
Use a variety of low-advanced academic English grammar, sentence structure, and vocabulary.
Integrate credible academic sources to support writing assignments, using basic citation.

rows.title: ESL Public Speaking and Advanced Pronunciation
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply critical thinking skills to develop and deliver logical, credible, and well-researched presentations.
Interact successfully using advanced-level English language oral communication skills in diverse academic contexts.
Produce spoken English with increasing accuracy in pronunciation, grammar, and vocabulary.
Present speeches with increasing confidence, effective nonverbal communication, and fluency in diverse academic contexts.

rows.title: ESL Literacy: Comprehensive
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Recognize a limited range of simple spoken English.
Use a limited number of English words to communicate orally in a range of familiar settings.
Recognize a limited range of simple written English.
Write letters of the English alphabet, numbers, and simple words and phrases.

rows.title: ESL Beginning 1-2 Multilevel
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify main ideas and key details in basic conversations in English in familiar contexts.
Communicate in basic conversations in familiar contexts, using beginning English language structures and vocabulary.
Identify main ideas and key details in simple written texts in English in familiar contexts.
Write basic sentences, using beginning English language structures and vocabulary.

rows.title: Beginning High 3 Abridged
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Interpret general meaning and some details of high-beginning spoken English on familiar topics.
Interpret general meaning and some details of high-beginning English written texts on familiar topics.
Produce English at a high-beginning level to communicate orally in familiar contexts.
Produce English at a high-beginning level to communicate in writing in familiar contexts.

rows.title: Intermediate Low 5
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify main ideas and key details in a range of short, adapted spoken English texts on familiar topics.
Communicate orally in extended conversations and short discussions, using a limited range of low-intermediate English language structures and forms.
Identify main ideas and key details in short, adapted written English texts on familiar topics.
Write short paragraphs with main ideas and supporting details, using a limited range of low-intermediate English language structures and forms.
Work effectively in a diverse cultural environment at a low intermediate English level.

rows.title: Intermediate Low 6
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify main ideas and key details in a range of adapted spoken English texts on familiar and some unfamiliar topics.
Communicate orally in discussions, using a range of low-intermediate English language structures and forms.
Identify main ideas and key details in a range of adapted written English texts on familiar and some unfamiliar topics.
Write short, organized paragraphs with relevant ideas and details, using a range of low-intermediate English language structures and forms.
Work effectively in a diverse cultural environment at a low intermediate English level.

rows.title: ESL Intermediate High 7-8 Multilevel
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Interpret spoken English in a variety of adapted and authentic texts in familiar and unfamiliar contexts
Communicate in extended oral exchanges in various contexts, using high-intermediate English language structures and forms
Interpret written English in a variety of adapted and authentic texts in familiar and unfamiliar contexts
Compose developed, organized, multi-paragraph texts, using high-intermediate English language structures and forms
Work effectively in a diverse cultural environment at a high-intermediate level

rows.title: ESL Literacy: Abridged
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Recognize a limited number of simple spoken English words and phrases in familiar settings.
Use a limited number of words to communicate orally at a very basic level in familiar settings.
Identify letters of the English alphabet, numbers, and a limited number of simple, high-frequency words in familiar settings.
Write letters of the alphabet, numbers, and a limited number of simple, high-frequency English words.

rows.title: ESL Reading and Writing - Beginning High
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify main ideas and key details in a variety of simplified written texts in familiar contexts at a high-beginning English language (ESL) level.
Use high-beginning English language (ESL) level grammar, sentence structure, and vocabulary to compose short paragraphs.

rows.title: ESL Reading and Writing - Intermediate Low
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify main ideas and key details in a variety of adapted written English texts in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts at a low-intermediate English language (ESL) level.
Use low-intermediate English language (ESL) level grammar, sentence structure, and vocabulary to compose short, organized paragraphs with relevant support.

rows.title: ESL Conversation - Intermediate High
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate appropriately and effectively in extended conversations and discussions on a variety of current topics, using English at a high-intermediate ESL level.
Use high-intermediate English structures and vocabulary in extended conversational exchanges and discussions.

rows.title: ESL for Custodians
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply high-beginning level English language skills and strategies to communicate on the job in a custodial position.
Recognize basic workers’ rights.
Perform job search skills at a high-beginning English language level.

rows.title: ESL Speaking in Social and Work Settings
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply intermediate-level English language skills to oral communication in social situations, including everyday life and workplace settings.
Describe cultural differences in U.S. and student home cultures using intermediate-level English language skills.

rows.title: ESL Intermediate for Computer Keyboarding
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply oral and written instructions to complete typewritten communication at an intermediate English level.
Exhibit appropriate keyboarding skills in typing intermediate-level correspondence in English with speed and accuracy.

rows.title: ESL for Healthcare Careers
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply high intermediate English language skills to describing and evaluating the skills, responsibilities, and requirements for various healthcare professions.
Apply high intermediate English language skills to the analysis of the U.S. healthcare system and critical issues in healthcare.
Apply high intermediate English language skills and cultural humility when communicating with patients and co-workers in a professional, multicultural healthcare environment.

rows.title: Fundamentals of Air Conditioning and Refrigeration
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Relate the functions of compressors, evaporators, and condensers in a refrigeration system
Calculate refrigerating capacity for various refrigerants
Select refrigeration components appropriate for a given application
Summarize the operating controls of refrigeration equipment
Summarize the safety controls of refrigeration equipment

rows.title: Introduction to Ethnic Studies
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze race as a social construct and the changing definitions of race.

Examine the impact and histories of immigration, colonization, and diaspora in the shaping of ethnic and racial formations in the United States, including Native Americans, African Americans, Asian Americans, and Latinx Americans.
Assess historical roots and contemporary consequences of prejudice, discrimination, and institutional racism.

Describe and evaluate major theories of race and ethnicity, and how the intersections of social class, gender, sexuality, and ability pervade racial and ethnic identity formations in the United States.
Analyze representations in the popular press and other media that influence relations in ethnic and racial groups in American society.
Appraise and create artistic and cultural representations that speak to race and ethnicity in the United States.
Identify and evaluate social movements and/or policy debates for racial justice and equity.

rows.title: Apparel Construction II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Operate machinery properly and safely.
Plan pattern layouts and garment construction sequences to minimize waste.
Employ appropriate seams, edge finishes, hand stitches, fastenings or closures.
Apply complex construction sequences and modular construction techniques in sewing multiple types of garments, using challenging fabrics.

rows.title: Flat Pattern Design I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze garment design components and interpret them using the principles of flat pattern making
Create patterns that accurately represent the original design and fit the intended model
Create patterns that include various garment elements such as bodices, skirts, dresses, sleeves, and collars
Integrate standard industry markings and symbols into garment patterns

rows.title: Fashion Illustration II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply illustration and rendering techniques to the fashion figure using advanced illustration techniques.
Evaluate mediums, color palettes and textiles used in clothing collections at an advanced level.
Create illustrations that communicate designs for a more specific intended customer demographic than in Illustration 1.
Create specification sheets for garment production at an advanced level.

rows.title: Introduction to the Fashion Industry
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compare how fashion evolves and changes in an economic, sociological, and political context.
Analyze and explain key factors and theories in the adoption of fashion.
Summarize the different roles of the designer, manufacturer and retailer in the fashion industry.
Examine the materials used in creating fashion.

rows.title: Creating a Garment Business
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Create a business plan for a fashion business concept.
Evaluate the feasibility of a fashion business concept by using common financial analysis.
Access the skills necessary for a successful entrepreneurial fashion business.
Conceptualize a fashion business concept that will solve a problem or need for a specific target group.

rows.title: Fashion Writing, Publicity, & Social Media
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Report on fashion trends exhibited at in-person events and events on social media platforms.
Evaluate and apply a variety of writing styles about fashion.
Assess the Bay Area fashion scene through research and personal observations.
Compose press releases for local fashion events or designer brands.
Create a fashion social media presence.

rows.title: Work Experience in Personal Styling
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the organization of the company in which the student is working, and compare the various job functions necessary to work in various positions.
Perform assigned essential job tasks under supervision in personal styling/image consulting.
Apply appropriate standards of conduct and personal presentation in the fashion workplace.

rows.title: Sewing with Knit and Stretch Fabrics
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the differences between woven and knitted fabrics, and between different types of knit fabrics.
Operate commonly used machinery for sewing on knits, including sergers and stretch stitch machines.
Design and construct garments made from knit fabrics using techniques that are unique and appropriate for those fabrics, such as ribbed and elastic finishes.

rows.title: Continuation of Elementary French
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate orally and argumentatively in French at the intermediate low-level.
Examine and interpret texts in French at the intermediate low-level, evaluating such factors as audience, purpose, and communication norms and strategies.
Compose written communications sharing thoughts and opinions in French at the intermediate low level.
Discuss the geography, history, and cultures of various Francophone countries and regions.

rows.title: Continuation of Elementary French
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate argumentatively and orally in French at the intermediate low-level
Examine and interpret texts in French at the intermediate low-level, evaluating factors such as audience, purpose, and communication norms and strategies
Compose written communications sharing thoughts and opinions in French at the intermediate low-level
Discuss the geography, history, and cultures of various Francophone countries and regions

rows.title: Culture and Civilization of France
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Relate historic events from the Roman occupation through the feudal period to early literature and architecture.
Relate Romanesque, Gothic, and Renaissance architecture to changes in French society in these periods.
Analyze religious and political influences on seventeenth and/or eighteenth century cultural artifacts.
Describe connections between the cultural developments of the nineteenth century and the political and historic events of the time.
Compare the central artistic role of nineteenth-century France to France's role today.

rows.title: Introduction to GIS
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe and utilize basic GIS software and geographic data in both vector and raster formats
Evaluate appropriate geographic data, metadata, and sources
Apply basic GIS techniques of spatial analysis, editing, geocoding, and geoprocessing
Create informative, clear, and cartographically correct maps

rows.title: World Regional Geography
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and explain the major concepts and approaches to the study of world regional geography.
Locate and describe the primary physical features of each of the world's major regions.
Evaluate human-environment interactions shaping the geographies of the world's major regions.
Compare political, cultural, and economic processes across the world's major regions.

rows.title: Introduction to Climate Change
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply scientific inquiry and investigation of evidence to critically evaluate climate change principles.
Communicate climate and climate change ideas and theories effectively.
Apply scientific principles, theories, or models to explain climate and climate change phenomena.
Evaluate human interactions with climate and the societal impacts.

rows.title: Historical Geology with Lab
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Investigate geologic phenomena through a variety of scientific inquiry techniques.
Apply scientific inquiry and the investigation of evidence to critically evaluate scientific arguments relating to historical geology.
Communicate historical geology ideas and theories effectively.
Apply geologic, stratigraphic, and fossil principles, theories, or models to interpret ancient environments, paleoclimates, and plate tectonic settings.
Evaluate the ways in which historical geology principles and data impact society and how living organisms have impacted and continue to impact our planet.

rows.title: The San Andreas Fault System
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Observe, describe, and analyze the physical forces and processes that have shaped the major topographical features found along the San Andreas fault system.
Collect and analyze rock, sediment, soil, and/or fossil samples and use them to develop working hypotheses about local fault processes.
Evaluate geologic hazards associated with the San Andreas fault system, and identify and evaluate what has been done to minimize the damage.
Review and evaluate the supporting data for the geological history of the San Andreas fault system.

rows.title: Introduction to Business
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe and apply business terminology and concepts.
Assess the impact of competition, metrics, and various economic systems within the context of a global economy.
Analyze the relationships among the various functional areas of a business, including finance, human resources, operations, and marketing.
Evaluate small business and entrepreneurship and their increased importance in the U.S. economy.

rows.title: Computer Applications in the Health Care Setting
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify the three types of computers commonly found in the health care setting, parts of a system, and various peripherals used in healthcare.
Analyze computer use in the healthcare setting related to data security, privacy, and confidentiality.
Create healthcare-related business documents and reports to include spreadsheets to present data in pivot tables and charts for clinical and financial reports.
Use a variety of software applications effectively in a health care setting.

rows.title: United States Women's History:  Pre-Colonial Through 1880s
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze and explain key social, cultural, political, and economic factors influencing the history of women in the United States from the pre-colonial period through the 1880s.
Describe and analyze the impact of race, class, and ethnicity on women's experience and status from the pre-colonial period through the 1880s.
Explain the major historical developments in United States women's history from the pre-colonial period through the 1880s.
Analyze, evaluate, and synthesize historical evidence and interpretations in writing, drawing on primary and secondary sources.

rows.title: History of Mexico
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Interpret the history of Mexico through social science and historical methodologies.
Explain the emergence of the indigenous world in Mesoamerica.
Analyze the major historical, political, economic, and social transformation that Mexico experienced during the colonial era.
Evaluate the current history of Mexico in a transnational and global context.
Compare the major social, political, economic, and cultural developments, their causes and effects in the history of modern Mexico.

rows.title: History of California
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Correlate the effects of the forces, events, and lives that have affected California's history.
Analyze the cultural, economic, social, and ideological factors that have influenced the development of California.
Identify, evaluate, and integrate primary and secondary source materials, to reach well-reasoned conclusions about California history.
Examine the artistic and cultural impacts of diverse peoples in their historical context in the history of California.

rows.title: History of San Francisco
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify the major individuals and events that have contributed to the political, cultural, and economic growth and development of San Francisco and analyze and assess their impact on the City's history.
Analyze the impact of the Gold Rush, the Silver strike, and the Transcontinental railroad on San Francisco's history and development and compare the impact of these watershed events..

Examine the impact of immigration and racial/ethnic groups on the development of San Francisco, including changes in politics, policies, culture, society, and the economic organization of the city of San Francisco.
Interpret San Francisco history primary and secondary sources as appropriate for support of an argument or interpretation.

rows.title: Immigrants in U.S. History
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze historical evidence from primary sources and interpretations from secondary sources of immigrant experiences in U.S. history.
Explain U.S. immigration history through various analytical categories.
Explain major economic, technological and scientific developments and their historical significance as they relate to immigrant experience in the United States.
Analyze major political, social, and cultural developments and trends, including both mainstream and reform efforts, and explain their historical significance as related to U.S. immigration.
Evaluate United States immigration in a global context.

rows.title: Medical Terminology II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Construct and de-construct medical terms using roots, prefixes and suffixes, and spell and pronounce medical terms of selected organ systems.
Interpret meanings and appropriate use of abbreviated and medical phrases based on context.
Interpret medical terminology in radiology, oncology, psychiatric, and other medical specialty reports.
Integrate and apply medical terminology words and abbreviations across the anatomy, physiology, pathology, diagnosis, and treatment of selected organ systems.

rows.title: Legal Aspects of Health Information Management
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the U.S. legal system, sources of law, branches of government, judicial process, and its impact on Health Information Management.
Analyze the legal health record and the procedures for access and disclosure of personal health information and the role of government and mandatory disclosure laws.
Compare risk management and quality improvement and the relationship to health information management.
Demonstrate compliance with external forces.
Apply legal processes and policy impacting healthcare.

rows.title: CPT Coding
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compare the various reimbursement systems in healthcare as they apply to commercial, government, and managed care health plans
Describe the sections, appendices, format, code conventions, section notes, and guidelines of the CPT code book
State the purpose of CPT and the Health Care Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) and its relationship to ICD-10-CM coding and billing claim forms
Interpret the health record documentation to identify services and procedures for coding purposes
Apply CPT codes, HCPCS codes, and modifiers to exercises and case studies

rows.title: Health and Aging
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Examine the social impacts of the expanding elderly population.
Analyze the impact of age-related biological and cognitive changes on functional abilities and service needs.
Analyze the impact of the social determinants of health and resilience on the overall well-being of aging adults from diverse communities.
Assess evidence-based interventions and services that support older adults to be cognitively, physically, and socially engaged.
Evaluate public policies in terms of their effects on older adults.
Research and critique theories of aging for their usefulness in explaining individual behavior and service needs.

rows.title: Internship Preparation and Professional Conduct in Mental Health
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply an understanding of wellness and recovery principles and counseling skills in behavioral health settings.
Analyze the expectations and responsibilities of professional conduct, service delivery, and field placement.
Assess the role that self-awareness and reflection play in professional growth and development.

rows.title: Statistics for Public Health
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze public health data utilizing statistical methods and tools used by public health professionals
Calculate and interpret descriptive and inferential statistics to understand public health data presented in textual, visual, and graphical formats
Discuss the advantages and limitations of public health statistical methods used to assess statistical significance.
Compare various types of study designs and sampling strategies used in public health

rows.title: CHW Principles & Practice 1
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze health issues and inequalities from public health and social justice perspectives.
Assess and apply professional skills and readiness for internship placement.
Discuss and demonstrate concepts and skills for providing person-centered (also known as client-centered) assessment, health education, counseling, and care management services.

rows.title: Community Birth Worker/Doula Education
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the role that doulas/community birth workers have in perinatal, childbirth, and postpartum care.
Explain the importance of birth work from a trauma-informed and community-centered approach.
Apply evidence-based and best-practice skills to support birthing people and their families.
Create a professional birth worker plan that utilizes local resources, systems and opportunities

rows.title: Men, Gender, and Health
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply gender role conflict theory to the analysis of masculinity and male gender construction.

Analyze the impact of the social determinants of health on the risk factors, prevention and treatment of illness and disease, and quality of health services for men of various races, ethnicities, gender identities, sexual orientations, and socioeconomic statuses.
Analyze behavior change theories and models as they relate to the complexity of men, gender and health.
Examine contemporary issues and ethics, including body image, substance use, sexuality, gender roles and expressions, aging, injury, and violence as they affect health.
Evaluate the credibility, reliability, and cultural appropriateness of health information, using qualitative and quantitative methods.

rows.title: Trauma, Resilience and Recovery
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain trauma, traumatic events, and common trauma responses at the individual and community levels.
Analyze strategies and resources to promote resiliency, recovery, and healing at the individual and community levels.
Apply client-centered counseling approaches for working with people with lived experience of trauma.
Integrate trauma-informed and trauma-transformed care into professional scope of practice.

rows.title: Personal and Community Health
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Distinguish personal health from public health and examine diverse dimensions of wellness in both.
Analyze social and behavioral factors and systems that influence the health of individuals and communities, including inequities.
Analyze personal and family health as it relates to aging, human sexuality, relationships, gender identity, sexual orientation, and parenthood.
Apply weight-inclusive and culturally-appropriate models to the promotion of physical activity, healthy eating, and dietary recommendations.
Examine prevention, treatment, health promotion, and advocacy strategies for wellness in the face of stress, addiction, violence, and other threats to health.
Evaluate sources of health information and research utilizing the scientific language of the discipline.

rows.title: Youth Development & Leadership
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Examine the relationship between the health of a community and the health of the young person through examining significant health and social issues that affect today's youth.
Assess the role of adolescent and human brain development in youth behavior and decision-making.
Evaluate cultural assumptions and stereotypes about young people and youth culture.
Apply principles of youth development and youth empowerment to the analysis of various youth development models.

rows.title: Case Management & Individual Counseling
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Appraise the process of case management, including the roles and responsibilities, ethical and professional responsibilities, and importance of cultural humility in counseling with substance-use disorder clients.
Demonstrate skills in interviewing, effective communication, self-care, and cultural humility.
Assess and apply client-centered skills to all phases of case management, including community-based referrals and linkages for effective case management.
Formulate and apply proficiency in case management practice through conceptualization, design, documentation and presentation of a mock client case file.

rows.title: Interpreting Lab I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Use basic to intermediate levels of interpreting skills to facilitate communication in health situations.
Apply healthcare interpreting skills at a moderate rate of speech.

rows.title: Community Nutrition and Education
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compare socioeconomic and cultural influences on food behavior and health outcomes in diverse communities.
Analyze nutritional guidelines and policies as well as their impact through a public health lens.
Integrate knowledge of food security, resources, cultural food habits, and weight-inclusive models in nutrition education and advocacy.
Provide person-centered support to promote health with individuals, groups, and communities.

rows.title: Hepatitis ABCs
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Distinguish between the different types of hepatitis characteristics and their treatment options
Evaluate the relationships between substance use, HIV, and viral hepatitis including Hep C and other emerging strands
Apply different models of public health practice as they relate to viral hepatitis

rows.title: Coaching Healthcare Interpreters
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze evidence-based concepts and models in coaching that support a growth mindset in learners.
Describe and create coaching lesson plans that are clear, purposeful, engaging, and student-centered.
Design interpreting skills activities that acknowledge sociocultural and linguistic nuances of working in a healthcare setting.

rows.title: Group Counseling for Treatment and Recovery
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:

Examine basic concepts of family systems and substance use dependency for supporting families in counseling.
Apply developmental stages and principles of group leadership to planning and facilitating groups.
Prepare and facilitate a group session based on wellness and recovery principles for diverse groups.

rows.title: Women in the Arts
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and critique established and emergent women artists in various disciplines.
Analyze the relationship between artists and their cultural and historical context of production.
Explain the obstacles and challenges women have faced in establishing themselves as artists.
Compare establishment media with traditional forms to question the distinction often drawn between crafts, with which women have been closely associated, and the fine arts.

rows.title: American Cultures in Literature and Film
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply literary and film terminology used in aesthetic evaluation and cultural criticism.
Analyze how the concept of the American dream has shaped cultural formations in the U.S. and beyond.
Assess historical and contemporary issues in the U.S. through cinematic and literary representations.
Evaluate the intersectionality of any two interlinking features of one’s social location as bases of oppression or privilege as depicted in American literature and film.

rows.title: Introduction to Museum Studies
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the creative and critical perspectives related to the history, design, and practices of museums in the United States in the last 100 years.
Assess the value and variety of the missions of museums in the context of local museum and exhibition resources.
Evaluate multicultural voices and visions in art, history, and science museum collections.
Analyze museum strategies for evoking and synthesizing personal transformation and community engagement.

rows.title: Poetry for the People
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze and appraise poetry from different racial/ethnic and social groups.
Compose and revise poems that demonstrate awareness of diverse cultural traditions.
Compare the aesthetic features of poetic traditions and forms from diverse cultures across time.
Design and execute a project that takes poetry to the community.

rows.title: Fa'a Pasefika: Interdisciplinary Cultural Expressions of Oceania
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify the centrality of the ocean aesthetic across Pacific Islander cultural practices.
Evaluate artistic and creative works that emerge from the experience of the sea.
Analyze how forms of social oppression shape artistic expressions across Oceania.
Produce works of cultural and artistic expressions that speak to social justice issues.

rows.title: Diversity and Social Justice: Heterosexism
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe and analyze heterosexism as a system of oppression and privilege.
Assess biases and stereotypes in relation to heterosexism.
Examine individual and collective ways of taking action against heterosexism.
Explain the intersectionality of heterosexism with other distinct forms of social oppression.

rows.title: Diversity: Ageism and Adultism (Age-based Oppression)
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe and analyze systems of oppression and privilege related to age.
Assess age-based biases and stereotypes.
Examine individual and collective ways of taking action in response to age-based bias and discrimination.
Explain the intersectionality of age-based discrimination with other distinct forms of social oppression.

rows.title: Global History of Interior Design
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply visual environmental literacy through the analysis of different periods and movements of interior design.
Compare the characteristics of each design movement and their influence upon other movements and designers.
Identify the characteristics of various historical periods and movements of interior design.

rows.title: Continuation of Intermediate Conversational Italian
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES

Apply intermediate-mid level skills in listening comprehension of Italian.
Explain elements of the history, culture, and social trends of the Italian-speaking world.

rows.title: Continuation of Elementary Italian
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES

Read and write in Italian at an elementary level.

Explain and compare elements of Italian culture at an elementary level.

rows.title: Continuation of Intermediate Italian

Assess and articulate aspects of Italian culture responsively at an intermediate-high level.

Apply a cultural understanding of Japanese syllabic writing systems and Kanji at a pre-basic beginning level when composing short communications
Describe basic elements of Japanese culture in relation to diverse communication practices.

rows.title: Continuation of Elementary Japanese Part II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate orally at an advanced beginning level in Japanese.
Interpret the main ideas and grammatical forms of a written text in Japanese at an advanced beginning level.
Compose short communications in the Japanese syllabic writing systems and Kanji at an advanced beginning level.
Explain elements of Japanese culture.

rows.title: Intermediate Japanese Part II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES

outcomes: Communicate orally at a basic intermediate level in Japanese.
Interpret the main ideas and grammatical forms of a written text in Japanese at a basic intermediate level.

Discuss various aspects of Japanese culture.

rows.title: Introduction to Contemporary Media
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:

Evaluate the history, technological evolution, and functions of the mass media with emphasis on the news media in the U.S.
Assess the behavioral impact of the mass media on society.
Analyze the influence of media ownership on news coverage.
Analyze global mass media systems.

rows.title: News Production and Publication I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify journalistic standards and expectations for a news publication
Describe the editorial and operational structure of a campus news publication
Evaluate whether the campus publication meets the information needs of its audience
Create a basic portfolio of published works for employment opportunities in the field of journalism

rows.title: Intermediate Magazine Editing and Production
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Develop various types of writing, editing, photography, illustration and/or design content for a magazine at an intermediate level.
Evaluate the quality of content and design expected in a college news and feature publication.
Edit content to make it suitable for publication in a college news and feature publication.
Produce a college news and feature publication using best journalism principles and practices.

rows.title: Intermediate Photojournalism
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES

outcomes: Apply skills in photographic storytelling, reporting, and editing at an intermediate level.
Analyze and describe the various current forms of multimedia technology platforms and media outlets used by professional photojournalists.
Integrate tools needed for the execution of multimedia options necessary for the professional development of photojournalists.
Synthesize creative and technical aspects of photojournalism skills into a digital portfolio.

rows.title: Latin American Social Movements

Synthesize the relationship between the state, the market, and civil society in Latin America.
Analyze the impact of globalization on democracy and social movements in Latin America.
Appraise the role identity plays in the constitution of the new social movements.

rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES

rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
