rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Measure modern physics data and evaluate uncertainties with specialized experimental apparatus.
Report on procedural methods, evidence, uncertainties, and conclusions of modern physics laboratory exercises.
Assess and present relationships between results of real-world laboratory exercises and modern physics theory.

rows.title: Introduction to Public Policy
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the role that governmental structures, political processes, and political actors play in the public policy-making process.
Evaluate public policies and alternative policy approaches.
Create public policy recommendations using the tools of policy analysis.
Explain the steps in the public policy process.
Analyze overall trends in policy formulation in the United States.

rows.title: Environmental Politics and Policy
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain environmental politics and policy in the United States, including their historical development.
Appraise the role of environmental issues and politics in international relations using International Relations theories.
Compare environmental politics and policy in other countries using comparative political science approaches.
Analyze and express basic concepts of environmental political theory, including ecofeminism and non-Western perspectives.

rows.title: The Constitution and Individual Rights
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the law with a general knowledge of its basic principles and applications.
Distinguish and evaluate the individual's legal rights and privileges and how to protect them.
Compare the various types of law.
Define and analyze constitutional amendments, rights, and limitations.

rows.title: Abnormal Psychology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Summarize the challenges and benefits in establishing and applying criteria for psychological abnormality.
Evaluate and debate the methods currently used to assess and diagnose psychological abnormality.
Analyze the symptoms and functional impacts of major psychological disorders.
Compare the major theoretical models used to understand the etiology and treatment of abnormal behavior.
Analyze and assess the impact of sociocultural factors on the assessment, diagnosis, and prevalence of mental disorders.

rows.title: Psychology of Eating, Food, and Weight
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the biopsychosocial relationship between emotions, cognitions, and behaviors and eating, food, and weight through analysis of current research.
Explain the etiologies, treatments, and cross cultural variations of major eating disorders.
Differentiate and personally redefine common misconceptions related to eating, food, and weight.

rows.title: Psychology of Race and Ethnic Relations
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the impact of race and ethnicity on affect, cognition, and behavior.
Evaluate current research on the psychology of race and ethnicity.
Analyze how prejudice and racism shape the dynamics of relations across and within racial and ethnic groups.
Identify psychological outcomes associated with racial and ethnic identity.
Distinguish the psychological consequences of racism for both the oppressed and oppressing groups.

rows.title: Social Psychology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe research methods and major scientific studies conducted in social psychology.
Integrate theoretical perspectives and concepts used in social psychology to explain human behavior and mental processes in social situations.
Analyze the ways in which an individual’s thoughts, feelings, and behaviors influence and are influenced by other people, sociocultural factors, and/or aspects of the physical environment.
Apply social psychology to explain everyday problems and real-world issues.

rows.title: Psychology of Psychoactive Drugs
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply basic terms and concepts in psychopharmacology.
Evaluate research findings related to psychoactive drugs for research design, implications and limitations of findings.
Compare the psychological effects of various drug categories.
Debate contrasting perspectives on benefits and risks of drug use and societal drug policies.

rows.title: Fire Training Work Experience I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply Firefighter I knowledge and skills to emergency and non-emergency situations.
Analyze dangerous situations and assist with retrieving appropriate tools and equipment for fire personnel.
Use tools and equipment according to the National Fire Protection Association's Standard 1001 for Firefighter I.
Explain the importance of teamwork at emergency incidents and non-emergency training.
Understand that all civilians and patients must be treated equally with respect.

rows.title: Basic Fire Academy
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Assess patient status and apply the correct basic life support interventions to patients with a variety of emergency medical and traumatic conditions, in accordance with local and national EMT protocols.
Apply job knowledge and performance skills of the current State Fire Training Firefighter One curriculum for firefighting and rescue.
Apply job knowledge and performance skills of the current State Fire Training Firefighter One curriculum for wildland fire fighting.
Apply job knowledge and performance skills of the current State Fire Training Firefighter One curriculum for hazardous materials.
Apply job knowledge and performance skills of the California Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) and SFFD fire apparatus driving.

rows.title: Introduction to Homeland Security
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the history of the threat of terrorism and threats to the homeland.
Examine the role of intelligence and counterintelligence within the homeland security discipline.
Analyze the proper steps ranging from mitigation to recovery for all-hazards events.
Describe how the roles of risk communication, warning communication, and crisis communication assist with the mission of homeland security.
Analyze the future role and challenges for homeland security.

rows.title: Fire Tactics and Strategy
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify the duties and requirements of the company officer in a fire suppression company on the fire ground.
Apply management principles of operational strategy and tactics in emergency situations.
Explain the skills and concepts applicable to the position of company officer in engine and truck companies and other specialized fire apparatus.
Apply basic knowledge of fire behavior and types of structures and occupancies as they pertain to the role of the company officer.
Identify operational management principles in emergency situations when in overall command of an incident or when working in other supportive command functions.

rows.title: Principles of Fire and Emergency Services: Safety and Survival
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Assess whether counseling, psychological, and wellness support programs are appropriate and available for emergency services personnel and their families.
Determine if adopting standardized policies for responding to emergencies can minimize near misses, injuries, and deaths.
Employ concepts of risk management to avoid near-misses, injuries, or line-of-duty deaths.
Evaluate the need for national training standards as they correlate to professional development inclusive of qualifications, certifications, and re-certifications.
Explain how the investigation of near-misses, injuries, and line-of-duty deaths can support cultural change throughout emergency services.

rows.title: Fire Behavior and Combustion
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze why fire starts and spreads
Prioritize the numerous hazardous products of combustion
Differentiate the five classes of fire and their relationship to proper application of extingishing agents
Compare fire control techniques

rows.title: Company Officer 2C: Fire Inspections and Investigations
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Perform a fire inspection in compliance with the policies of the authority having jurisdiction (AHJ) and prepare the proper documentation for recording and initiating the approved corrective action
Describe construction, alarm, detection, and suppression features that contribute to or prevent the spread of fire, heat, and smoke throughout a building
Explain the steps that need to be taken to secure an incident scene to keep unauthorized persons from restricted areas and to preserve evidence from damage or destruction
Describe how to identify the area of origin or point of origin of the fire and make a preliminary determination of the cause of the fire

rows.title: Introduction to Sociology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Distinguish and interpret the major contemporary sociological perspectives.
Analyze and distinguish the basic conceptual tools of sociology.
Evaluate and apply concepts from areas of sociological interest to current social issues.
Utilize critical thinking and applications from the discipline of sociology to examine real life situations.
Define the techniques of sociological research.

rows.title: Sociology of Deviance and Crime
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compare major theoretical perspectives on deviance and the sociology of crime.
Apply sociological analytical tools to the analysis of human behavior and methods for measuring crime rates.
Apply theoretical perspectives to the analysis of societal reactions to deviance pursued by institutions.

rows.title: Sex, Marriage, and Family Relationships
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Categorize and trace the social forces that shape family structure and dynamics in the United States from its inception to the present.
Articulate the socially constructed meanings of marriage and family, including their related components.
Analyze how major social institutions and practices influence personal choices regarding the institution of family.
Analyze the impact of social characteristics on family practices, structures, and dynamics using intersectional frameworks.

rows.title: Elementary Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate in Spanish at a novice-high level with accurate grammatical structure, intelligible pronunciation, and intonation
Interpret the main ideas of a written text in Spanish at a novice-high level
Compose short written communications incorporating the principles of past and present tense syntax at a novice-high level
Articulate aspects of the cultures of the Spanish-speaking world areas and communities

rows.title: Continuation of Intermediate Conversational Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate effectively in Spanish at an intermediate high level, expressing opinions and contrasting ideas and concepts when confronted with cultural and social aspects of the analyzed works

Analyze several important films from Spanish-speaking countries at an intermediate high level, comparing different technical, artistic, and cultural aspects with an understanding of the value and intentions of creative expression.
Explain socio-economic and cultural aspects of Spanish-speaking countries as presented in films with a broad understanding of social constructs.

rows.title: Grammar Review and Composition
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Recognize and use complex structures to interact orally in Spanish at near-native level.
Use accurate Spanish grammar, punctuation, and syntax when producing or summarizing texts.
Interpret complex structures and idioms from original media in Spanish.
Describe examples of literary, historical, and contemporary influences in the Spanish-speaking world.

rows.title: Continuation of Elementary Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate orally in Spanish at a mid-intermediate level with accurate grammatical structures, intelligible pronunciation, and intonation.
Interpret the main ideas of a written text in Spanish at a mid-intermediate level.
Compose short written communications incorporating the principles of Spanish grammar and syntax at a mid-intermediate level.
Compare aspects of Latin America and Spanish Peninsular cultures and societies.

rows.title: Spanish for Heritage Speakers 1B
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Assess the grammar and syntax structures of the language by applying them to professional settings.
Communicate in writing with a broad range of vocabulary related to topics of personal, public, and community interest, applying enriched vocabulary and grammar proficiency.
Communicate and express with detail and organization on familiar and some new concrete topics using high-frequency structures and personalized vocabulary that facilitate comprehension.
Describe and compare cultural aspects of Spanish-speaking countries as well as Spanish-speaking groups in the United States.

rows.title: Intermediate Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate in Spanish at an intermediate level with accurate grammatical structure, intelligible pronunciation, and clear intonation.
Interpret the main idea of a written text in Spanish at an intermediate level.
Analyze and compose short written communications in Spanish at an intermediate level.
Assess and articulate aspects of Latin American and Spanish Peninsular cultures responsively at an intermediate level.

rows.title: Advanced Spanish: Hispanic Culture and Civilization
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate effectively in Spanish about Hispanic cultures.
Analyze critically significant issues of each chronological period of Hispanic civilization from the Golden Age to the Present.
Identify historical figures and moments of the Hispanic cultures and civilization from the Golden Age to the Present.
Compare Spanish, Hispanic American, and Hispanic cultures from the Golden Age to the Present.

rows.title: Introduction to Statistics
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Assess how data were collected and recognize how data collection affects what conclusions can be drawn from the data.
Identify appropriate graphs and summary statistics for variables and relationships between them and correctly interpret information from graphs and summary statistics.
Describe and apply probability concepts and distributions.
Demonstrate an understanding of, and ability to use, basic ideas of statistical processes, including hypothesis tests and confidence interval estimation.
Identify appropriate statistical techniques and use technology-based statistical analysis to describe, interpret, and communicate results.
Evaluate ethical issues in statistical practice.

rows.title: Vocational Foundation Skills--Reading and Writing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply vocabulary to workplace communication
Interpret information and intentions in written instructions
Write instructions or reports to explain tasks, projects and incidents in the workplace
Use references and websites related to employment and jobs
Employ basic technology skills necessary for workplace communication

rows.title: Visual Media Digital Skills
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Define and use the major components of the Macintosh operating system.
Use font management software to organize and activate digital fonts.
Use industry-standard software to create basic graphics and animations.
Construct and publish basic layouts for print and web.

rows.title: Graphic Design I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply an iterative design process to various design problems.
Select and use elements and principles to convey a specific message to a defined audience.
Identify basic components of typographic form and function.
Create a unified and communicative composition incorporating type and/or image using appropriate techniques.
Appraise and evaluate student work through in-class verbal and written critiques.

rows.title: User Interface Design
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Discuss user-centered design considerations for a variety of interactive products and contexts.
Apply information architecture, visual hierarchy, type, color, motion and design patterns to interface designs for a range of products and platforms.
Apply interaction design principles, including associations, affordances, economy of motion, response and flow designs for a range of products and platforms.
Employ critical thinking and communication skills in the development of user interface solutions.
Employ and document an iterative design process.

rows.title: Web Production I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Create web pre-production documents, including site maps, mockups, and wire frames.
Evaluate the effectiveness of website projects.
Use industry-standard tools to create web content.
Employ soft skills that define a professional in the industry, including working with others and communicating clearly.

rows.title: InDesign I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the major components of the Adobe InDesign interface.
Construct basic InDesign documents according to industry best practices in typesetting and layout standards.
Employ document components to reproduce and package a document in InDesign.

rows.title: Storytelling and Storyboarding
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze different forms of narrative and describe the narrative structure as it applies to storytelling
Analyze the use of storyboards in the creation of narratives
Analyze the content, context, and thematic elements of preexisting texts
Create storyboards from original ideas and scripts
Create individual, detailed narratives and related storyboards.

rows.title: Portfolio Preparation
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Design and produce a professional online and sequenced portfolio of work matched to their goals
Develop and execute a self-directed timetable for refining and showcasing a series of portfolio projects
Write and design a curriculum vitae appropriate for furthering personal goals
Present themselves and their portfolio in a professional manner

rows.title: Design Studio Practicum II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Lead group verbal critiques and give meaningful feedback to others.
Manage other students in complex design projects requiring multiple contributors.
Work independently on projects while meeting deadlines and developing relevant and meaningful design solutions.

rows.title: Fundamentals of Nursing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the historical background of nursing, including how the role of the LVN has evolved over time.

Analyze basic concepts in nursing, including legal and ethical issues, HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act), confidentiality, nursing process, communication skills, documentation, and patients’ rights.
Apply evidence-based practice in performing the necessary nursing interventions appropriate for the clients' condition.
Perform fundamental nursing skills and demonstrate various physical assessment techniques utilizing the appropriate plan of care according to findings.
Perform basic nursing skills and complete each procedure accurately, prioritizing nursing care based on appropriate clinical judgment and critical thinking skills.

rows.title: Psychology in Nursing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compare historical and current perspectives on psychology related to nursing.
Explain the legal and ethical aspects of mental health nursing care, including client rights, confidentiality, and treatment appropriateness.
Determine how neuroscience relates to nursing care of clients with mental and psycho-physiological health challenges.
Provide professional and therapeutic communication in all aspects of the vocational nursing role.
Identify appropriate nursing responsibilities for clients suffering from stress, crisis, and abuse and determine the common defense and coping mechanisms.
Identify different types of mental, behavioral, mood, neurocognitive, and personality disorders, as well as nursing implications and appropriate treatments.

rows.title: Advanced Medical Surgical and Community Health Nursing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Differentiate between types and stages of shock, its potential complications, and appropriate nursing interventions utilizing reasonable clinical judgment and critical thinking.
Compare right- and left-sided heart failure, upper and lower airway disorders leading to respiratory failure and acute renal failure versus chronic renal failure.
Distinguish forms of cancer affecting gastrointestinal, hematological, lymphatic, neurological, and reproductive health and describe the implications for nursing in response to those distinct forms.
Describe the development of community health nursing, including the history of nursing elements of practice roles and functions.

Describe the LVN scope of practice established by the California Board of Vocational Nursing and Psychiatric Technicians (BVNPT) and nursing responsibilities in home health settings, long-term care, rehabilitative nursing, and during disasters.

rows.title: Our Stories
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Investigate creative storytelling and oral history research methods through the lens of intersectionality.
Examine creative storytelling as a transformative social, cultural, political, and historical practice.
Apply feminist theory to stories related to social, political, and economic issues.
Produce creative and ethnographic storytelling work informed by technical guidelines.

rows.title: Ending Sexual Violence: Peer Education
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze major forms of power abuse in intimate relationships
Analyze the interaction between dominant culture stereotypes and false explanations for sexual violence
Evaluate the effectiveness of a local community based organization addressing the problem of sexual violence
Apply principles of peer education and feminist consciousness raising in the preparation of facilitation plans
Apply varied peer education methods in the facilitation of a presentation on sexual violence prevention
